source_text: Quod quidem videns contra te valere plurimum, quasi ipso testimonio interrogatus: Per quid ergo parvuli in regno sunt adversariae potestatis, si Scripturae creditur unumquemque, cum vincitur, tunc servum esse victoris, et constat infantiam sine usu rationis et voluntatis nec confligere potuisse, nec cedere?, addis: "r unum quippe hominem peccatum intravit in mundum, et per peccatum mors; et ita in omnes homines pertransiit, in quo omnes peccaverunt " [n305] . Sic est autem Deus nascentium conditor, ut omnes ex uno eant in condemnationem, quorum non fuerit renascentium liberator. Ipse quippe dictus est "gulus ex eadem massa faciens vas, aliud in honorem secundum misericordiam, aliud in contumeliam secundum iudicium " [n306] , cui cantat Ecclesia: "Misericordiam et iudicium " [n307] . Hoc quod dicis, per unum hominem intrasse peccatum, quo testimonio Apostoli plurimorum ineruditorum tamen pectora commovistis, licet in quarto libro breviter quomodo intellegendum esset ostenderim [n308] , tamen adiuvante Christo, in hoc opere plenius exponemus, ita ut in secundo libro, praetermissis aliis, locus ipse apostolicus contextu suo plenissime disseratur.
pass_a_gloss: Which indeed seeing to avail most against you, as if asked by the testimony itself: Through what therefore are little ones in the kingdom of an adversary power, if it is believed to Scripture that each one, when he is conquered, is then a slave of the victor, and it stands that infancy without the use of reason and of will could neither clash, nor yield?, you add: Through one human indeed sin entered into the world, and through sin death; and so it passed through unto all humans, in whom all sinned. So however is God founder of those being born, that all go from one into condemnation, of whom he shall not have been the liberator of those being reborn. He himself indeed has been said a potter from the same mass making a vessel, one unto honor according to mercy, another unto insult according to judgment, to whom the Church sings: Mercy and judgment. This which you say, that through one human sin entered, by which testimony of the Apostle you have moved the breasts of very many unlearned nevertheless, although in the fourth book I briefly showed how it would have to be understood, nevertheless with Christ helping, in this work we will expound more fully, so that in the second book, other things having been passed over, the apostolic place itself may be discussed most fully by its own context.

pass_b_english: Seeing that this weighs heavily against you, you act as though the testimony itself had asked: “How, then, are infants in the kingdom of the hostile power, if we believe Scripture that each person becomes the victor's slave when he is defeated, and if infancy, without the use of reason and will, plainly could neither fight nor surrender?” (Psalm 101:1;) You add: “For through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death; and so it passed to all human beings, in whom all sinned” (Romans 5:12). You continue: “God is the Creator of newborn children in such a way that all go from the one into condemnation unless he becomes their liberator through rebirth. For he is called ‘the potter making from the same lump one vessel for honor according to mercy, another for dishonor according to judgment’ (Romans 9:21), to whom the Church sings, ‘Mercy and judgment’” (Psalm 101:1; LXX Psalm 100:1; Augustine, On Marriage and Concupiscence 2.8).

As for your statement that sin entered through one human being, the apostolic testimony by which you have stirred many hearts, though uneducated ones, I briefly showed in my fourth book how it should be understood. Yet with Christ's help we will explain it more fully in this work. In the second book we will set other things aside and discuss that apostolic passage most fully in its own context (see below, Book II, section 20).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: The source note links are misaligned here. The actual quotations identify Romans 5:12, Romans 9:21, and Psalm 101:1 (LXX Psalm 100:1), respectively. Source notes 305–307 instead point to Romans 9:21, Psalm 100:1, and Isaiah 45:9. The references in this translation follow the quoted words; Isaiah 45:9 is a possible background parallel for the potter image, not the source of “mercy and judgment”.
